findings.title: WASD at the bench pulls fitted parts out of their sockets (A = 'take out ACROSS MOTOR')
findings.problem: At the bench the station grabs the keyboard before walking does (src/game.ts:164), and the garage maps KeyA/KeyS/KeyD to the three sockets (src/stations/garage/station.ts:330-331). act('slot') with nothing held and a part already fitted removes the part (station.ts:206). So a player who has just fitted the flyback diode and reaches for WASD to walk away, which is the first thing anyone does in a third-person game, silently unfits it. I reproduced this in 02-wrong.mjs: with the diode fitted across the motor, pressing W then A gave slots {} and put the diode back in the tray (shot 49: 'Across motor —', prompt 'A Empty socket'). W does nothing, A and S remove parts, D removes the capacitor. The player then presses P, sees the 77 V reset again and believes the fix stopped working. That wrongly teaches that the diode doesn't help. It breaks DR-22 (the same key means the same verb everywhere; here A means 'walk' in the room and 'unplug' at the bench) and DR-19 (the key does something the player never asked for). It is not a soft-lock, but it quietly undoes progress and causes confusion.
findings.fix:
Pick one of these in station.ts key():
(a) Treat KeyW/KeyA/KeyS/KeyD and the arrow keys at the bench as 'stand up' (call game.leaveBench()), as E and Esc already do. Move the socket keys to Z/X/C or 7/8/9, and update SLOT_KEYS (station.ts:59) and hoverHint.
(b) Keep A/S/D, but have them only fit a held part, never remove one. Removal stays on click or Backspace: in act('slot'), return false when nothing is held and the call came from a key.
Also apply the same audit to the arcade bench, which also maps A/S/D.
findings.verify: New Playwright case in tests/station-garage.spec.ts: setUp, then pick diode, slot fly, then press KeyW, KeyA, KeyS, KeyD. Expect station.slots.fly to still be the diode (option b), or atBench false with the diode still fitted (option a). Retake garage-play-49.
findings.verify_reason: Reproduced. With the diode fitted across the motor, KeyW did nothing and KeyA emptied the socket: slots went from {fly:diode} to {}, and the prompt changed to 'P Pulse the motor' (verify log, shot verify-garage-play-06-after-W-A.jpg). In code, game.ts:164 sends every key to station.key() before walking sees it, station.ts:331 maps A/S/D to slot, and station.ts:206 removes a fitted part when nothing is held. The arcade bench has the same A/S/D mapping (src/stations/arcade/station.ts:353). Both proposed fixes are sound.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/tools/verify-garage-play/01-verify.mjs log: fitted {fly:diode} → after W same → after A {}

findings.title: Carried robot tips onto its side, floats beside Pip's head, and the marker cone pierces it
findings.problem: The delivery robot is a 'cart' prop with mass 8 (src/props/prefabs.ts:16), so it uses the 'light' carry. The body is driven to 1.05 m ahead at y = Pip+0.55 with angvel zeroed, but its rotation is never corrected (src/game.ts:330-331). While Pip lifts and turns, contacts tip the 1.2 × 0.65 × 0.75 box. In the zoom-9 orbit shots the teal robot hangs at about 70° with its wheels and underside toward the camera, beside and above Pip's head, held by one outstretched mitt (shots 74 and 08). In the game-camera shots 09 and 10 it reads as a tilted yellow block at head height. The objective marker is pinned to the robot's own translation (station.ts:97) and sits 2.1 m up, so the yellow cone pokes through the carried robot (shots 08, 73, 74). The robot is the hero of the room, the only thing Pip carries, and the thing that drives off at the end, so this is the most-seen model moment in the job. It breaks DR-65 (carried items sit level in front of the chest in both mitts, never beside or intersecting the head) and DR-44 (the marker sits above clutter, not inside the held item).
findings.fix:
Pick one:
(1) Make the robot a push-along item. Add `heavy:true` to its PropSpec, or give the 'robot' id mass ≥ 15 in level props, so it takes the existing 'heavy furniture is pushed along the floor so it stays upright' branch (game.ts:331): wheels on the floor, Pip pushing a rolling robot. That fits the fiction and the wheel spin can animate while it moves.
(2) Keep lifting, but in the carry branch slerp the body rotation each step to an upright quaternion around Pip's heading (b.setRotation(slerp(current, yawOnly(heading)), true)), lower the target to Pip.y+0.25, and reduce `ahead` to 0.75.
Either way, the marker must not sit on the held item (see the marker finding).
findings.verify: Retake garage-play-73/74 (zoom 9, orbit ±350 while carrying). The robot's up vector must have dot((0,1,0)) > 0.95, and its bounding box must not intersect a 0.3 m sphere at Pip's head (y 1.4). Add a spec assertion on the held robot's rotation after walking 3 m.
findings.verify_reason: Reproduced. In the zoom-9 orbits while carrying, the robot hangs at about 60–70° with its wheels and underside facing the camera, beside and above Pip's head, and the yellow marker cone sits on it (verify-03, verify-04). At the game camera it reads as a tilted block at head height (verify-02). The code matches: game.ts:331 drives linvel toward p.y+0.55 and 1.05 m ahead, zeroes angvel and never corrects rotation; prefabs.ts:16 gives cart mass 8, so it takes the light carry. Fix (1) is technically wrong as written: PropSpec has no `heavy` field, and mass is per kind (prefabs[kind].mass), not per id, so you can't give 'robot' mass ≥ 15 in the level props.
findings.fix_correction: For option (1), add a dedicated 'robot' PropKind in src/props/prefabs.ts (size about [1.2,.65,.75], mass ≥ 15) and use it in src/levels/garage.ts:8. Alternatively, have game.ts:331 also treat spec.id==='robot' as heavy. Note that heavy also blocks jumping (game.ts:180), which is fine for this item. Option (2) (slerp to an upright yaw-only quaternion, lower and closer target) is fine as written.

findings.title: Step-1 marker follows the robot in Pip's arms instead of pointing at the test stand
findings.problem: The first step's marker is `at:()=>this.bot?.body.translation()??PAD` (station.ts:97). Once Pip picks the robot up, the bouncing arrow rides on the carried robot, right over Pip's head (shots 07, 08, 73, 74), and never shows where to take it. The only destination cues are the card's words 'test stand behind the bench', a 1.2 m 'TEST STAND' plaque behind the bench, and a 'Set the robot on the stand' prompt that only appears within 2.6 m. The stand is a dark 2 × 1.3 m slab hidden behind the bench and scope from the default camera (shot 06). A new player carrying the robot has no world pointer to the goal. Meeting already handles this correctly ('held strip → marker at the door', src/ui/objectives.ts:33). This breaks DR-42 (the marker points at the current step's object, here the destination) and DR-13 (the target is never hidden: the stand sits behind the bench).
findings.fix: In station.ts step 1, use `at:()=>this.game.held===this.bot?STAND:(this.bot?.body.translation()??PAD)`. While the robot is held, also light the stand: swap the hazard-edge material to `hot()`, or pulse a ring decal (game.burst 'ring' every 1.5 s at STAND), so the drop zone is signposted from about 2.6 m (DR-14 style).
findings.verify: Carry the robot 2 m from the pad and read the marker position from a snapshot, or add `markerAt` to snapshot(). It must equal STAND (0.7, −4.45). Retake garage-play-07: the arrow is over the stand behind the bench, not over Pip.
findings.verify_reason: The marker does ride on the carried robot: station.ts:97 at()=bot translation, and the cone sits on the held robot in verify-02/03/04. One part is overstated. From the default game camera, the yellow 'TEST STAND' plaque above the stand is visible behind the bench (verify-02, garage-play-07), the card says 'test stand behind the bench', and the prompt changes to 'Set the robot on the stand' within 2.6 m (verify log). The destination is therefore not hidden. The bug is a wrong marker target with a cheap fix, not a blocker, so P2. The fix is correct (Meeting's held→destination pattern, objectives.ts:33).
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/shots/verify-garage-play-02-carry-game-cam.jpg (TEST STAND plaque visible, marker on robot)
verify log 'near stand': prompt 'E Set the robot on the stand'

findings.title: Win push-in frames the empty bench: the robot that just delivered is off-screen at the dock
findings.problem: The payoff of the whole job is the robot driving its route and stopping at the delivery dock (−8.1, −5.6), where the dock lamp turns green (room.ts:111-113). But game.winFocus() returns `station.table + 0.5` for every station (src/game.ts:398), and the push-in uses distance 7 and pitch 0.5 (game.ts:373). The win shot is therefore Pip cheering in front of a bench with 'Press PULSE' on the scope (shots 30, 32, 33). The robot, the dock and the green lamp are about 9 m away and out of frame. The result card then covers the right half. The celebration doesn't show what the player achieved. This breaks DR-11 (the win push-in frames Pip together with the working machine) and repeats the QA 10 class of bug ('Pip missing / wrong subject') for the garage.
findings.fix:
Add an optional `winFocus?():T.Vector3` to the Station interface (src/stations/types.ts). Make game.winFocus() prefer it. GarageBench returns the robot's final position (−8.1, 0.6, −5.6).
To keep Pip in frame as well, pick one:
(a) Make the last step 'Meet the robot at the dock'. Replace 'Watch the robot drive' with a step done when Pip is within 2.5 m of DOCK after `delivered`, so Pip is there for the push-in. This also removes the passive wait (next finding).
(b) Target the midpoint of Pip and the robot, with distance clamped to 7 + 0.6 × separation.
findings.verify: Retake garage-play-31/32 after win. The robot, the green dock lamp and Pip must all sit inside the centre 70 % of the frame (use the DR-11 bounds check from snapshot positions projected through the camera).
findings.verify_reason: Reproduced. 0.5 s after the win, the push-in frames the bench (scope reads 'Press PULSE'), the TEST STAND sign and an empty stand. The delivered robot, the dock and the green dock lamp at (−8.1, −5.6) are off-screen left, and the result card covers the right half (verify-15, verify-16). In code, game.ts:398 winFocus() returns station.table+0.5 for every station, and game.ts:373 offsets 2.2 m right with distance 7 and pitch 0.5. This breaks DR-11 as stated.

findings.title: The final 'Watch the robot drive' step is 9 s of passive waiting with a junk-prop prompt, and the robot bulldozes Pip with no reaction
findings.problem: After the third TEST, startDrive() kicks Pip off the bench (station.ts:256-261). The robot then drives the 27.9 m ROUTE at 3.2 m/s plus 0.8 s (station.ts:56-57), which is about 9.5 s of locked waiting: clean run, drive started at 37.5 s and win at 46.5 s. The card says 'Watch the robot drive its delivery route'. There is nothing to do, and the robot isn't framed, because the camera stays on Pip at the bench (shots 27-29). The prompt falls back to the nearest prop, 'E Grab the cone' or 'E Grab the bin' (src/ui/objectives.ts:82-83; shots 27, 64). When I stood Pip on the painted lane, the kinematic robot shoved him about 4 m along the route and then sideways (03-chaos.mjs log: Pip z −1.02 → 2.98 between drive ticks 3 and 7; shots 64, 65). There was no stumble, beep, sound or coworker reaction. It could have been the room's best slapstick moment, and today it's a non-event. This breaks DR-09 (no locked wait longer than 3 s), DR-42 (the prompt points at junk during the final step) and DR-03/DR-04 (physical comedy that the world ignores).
findings.fix:
(1) Make the last step active: 'Meet the robot at the dock' (see the win finding), with the marker on DOCK. The player races the robot, which is short and fun.
(2) While driving, have prompt() return null or a custom 'Follow the robot' pill instead of letting promptFor fall through to nearest(). Return a non-null prompt from the station while `driving`.
(3) Make contact funny. In update(), when the driving robot is within 0.9 m of Pip, play audio.voice('alarm') or a horn tone, give Pip a 0.3 s squash, apply an outward impulse, and burst 'star'. When it passes within 3 m of a coworker, game.alarm() or cheer.
(4) Optionally raise DRIVE_SPEED to 4.5 m/s, which gives about 7 s.
findings.verify: Time from the third TEST to won in the clean spec: the player is never idle for more than 3 s, or is following a live marker. Retake garage-play-64 with Pip on the lane: expect the alarm or squash reaction and a sound call (spy on audio.voice in a test).
findings.verify_reason: Partly confirmed. During the drive the prompt falls through to nearby clutter ('E Grab the bin'), and then to 'E Grab the cart' for the moving robot itself, because station.prompt returns null while driving (station.ts:454) and promptFor only stops at the station when atBench (objectives.ts:72). The kinematic robot shoves Pip along the lane with no reaction: in my log Pip z went −1.02 → 0.27 → 1.85 → 2.82 and then he slid sideways, with alarmed 0 throughout (verify-14). Two claims are wrong, though. The wait is not locked, because Pip can walk freely, so DR-09's 'locked wait' rule doesn't apply. And the robot is framed: at home zoom the room view shows the robot driving with the marker over it (garage-play-29). What remains is a missed gag plus a junk prompt during a victory lap, so P2, not P1.
extra_evidence: verify log drive 0-9: prompt 'E Grab the bin' then 'E Grab the cart' (the driving robot); alarmed 0
findings.fix_correction: Fix (2) needs a change in src/ui/objectives.ts:72 as well: station.prompt() returning null while not at the bench falls through to nearest(). Return a non-null 'Follow the robot' prompt from the station while driving, or exclude the driving robot from nearest().

findings.title: Job 3 prompt says '1–5 Change the parts' when the fix is the ground lever (G), not a part
findings.problem: After the job-3 PULSE captures a start-up brown-out, prompt() returns {key:'1–5', text:'Change the parts'} for any tier-0 verdict (station.ts:465). The fix in this job isn't a part: it's re-routing the controller's ground with the small blue-ball lever (key G), which is never named in any prompt unless the cursor happens to hover it (station.ts:447). So the key pill sends the player through the parts tray. The 1000 µF capacitor is the obvious-looking candidate, and it 'rides through part of it, but not enough' (spec line 'Job 3: a bulk capacitor ... but not enough'). That is a designed red herring, but the HUD actively pushes the player into it and gives no cue that the ground route is changeable. The lever is about 20 px at the bench camera and the 'GROUND: SHARED' plaque looks like a label, not a control (shot 24). Expected confusion: a cycle through all five parts and a failed TEST or two (each failed TEST is a mistake). This breaks DR-42 (the prompt points at the wrong thing) and DR-19 (the prompt isn't the real action). It also hurts DR-37: the ground route rule is hidden until stumbled on.
findings.fix:
In prompt(), pick the change hint from the verdict without naming the answer. For fault 'start', return {key:'1–5 · G', text:'Change the setup'}; keep '1–5' for the shutdown faults.
Make the lever read as a control:
- In buildBench, scale the lever ×1.8 and give it a yellow knob.
- After a 'start' capture, wiggle the lever (rotation.z ±0.15 for 0.6 s) the way the meeting coupler wobbles.
- Make the 'GROUND: SHARED' sign a hover target, so its hint shows G.
Also consider letting the player drag the controller's ground lead to the battery post physically (R4B redesign), which makes it a cable act (see the cable finding).
findings.verify: In a job-3 state after PULSE, read the .prompt-pill text: it must include 'G' or a non-parts wording. Retake garage-play-24: the lever is clearly visible and moves.
findings.verify_reason: Reproduced. After the job-3 PULSE (start brown-out), the pill reads '1–5 Change the parts' (verify-13, log 'job3 pulse'), as station.ts:465 does for any tier-0 verdict. The claim of 'no cue that the ground route is changeable' is overstated. The job-3 ask in the open panel says 'on a long ground wire shared with the motor', the panel row reads 'Ground: shared with motor', and the lever and 'GROUND: SHARED' plaque sit right beside the controller (verify-13). The pill is misleading, but strong world and panel cues exist, so P2.
extra_evidence: verify log 'job3 pulse': prompt '1–5 Change the parts'

findings.title: Every part has exactly one legal socket, so 'where does protection go' is never a decision; brute-forcing five parts solves every job
findings.problem: PARTS gives each part a single slot: diode→fly, clamp→fly, tvs→switch, snubber→switch, cap→ctrl (src/stations/garage/logic.ts:37-41). When a part is held, the only socket that fits glows (station.ts:270) and the prompt names its key ('A Fit it', station.ts:462; shot 17). Hovering any other socket says 'It does not fit here' (shot 46). The topology idea the sockets are named after (ACROSS MOTOR vs ACROSS SWITCH vs AT CONTROLLER) is therefore never chosen by the player. The only decisions are which of five parts, flip, and the ground lever. With PULSE free of mistakes (only TEST failures, shorts and a reversed cap count), a player can cycle 1-5 and P until the scope turns green, without understanding why. The ART/AGENTS goal 'play by doing, the mechanic is the concept' is weakened: the room shows the concept beautifully (beads circling the motor and diode loop, the arc at the switch) but the act is a menu pick. This breaks DR-26 (the concept is taught by a physical act, not by picking from a list) and DR-38 (trial and error reaches 'elegant').
findings.fix:
Let the diode-like parts fit both protection sockets. In logic.ts, set slots ['fly','switch'] for diode, clamp and tvs, and ['switch','fly'] for the snubber. The shutdown() solver already handles any thresholds in either place (flyChain for fly, the tvs branch for switch). It needs a generic diode-across-switch branch, using diodeI(x, fwd, rev) with the part's vf/vbr, in place of the TVS-only one.
Then a diode across the switch gives the coil no path, and a TVS across the motor clamps at about 45 V. Both are truthful and teach WHERE.
In prompt(), drop the socket letter from 'Fit it' and say 'A/S/D Fit it'. Keep the glow for every legal socket.
Charge a small credit per PULSE beyond the third in a job, so brute force shows on the cost axis (DR-38).
findings.verify: Unit test in logic.test.ts: judge(kickback, {switch:{part:'diode'}}) gives fault 'stop' (no path), and {fly:{part:'tvs'}} gives a clamp at about 45 V. Run the spec unchanged (the clean route still works). Retake garage-play-17: both protection sockets glow.
findings.verify_reason: Code-confirmed. logic.ts:37-41 gives each part exactly one slot, redraw glows only the legal pad (station.ts:270), the held-part prompt names that socket's key (station.ts:462), and hoverHint says 'It does not fit here' elsewhere (station.ts:445). WHERE is never a player decision. The physics in the fix is right: a TVS across the motor clamps the node at about 12+33 = 45 V, and a reverse diode across the low-side switch gives the coil no path. It needs solver work at logic.ts:115/129, where the switch branch currently only knows tvs and snubber.

findings.title: The robot's reboot (red eyes, dizzy wobble) faces away from the bench camera, and failure and pass moments are barely visible
findings.problem: The failure gag is the robot's controller rebooting: red eyes, a dizzy wobble and stars (station.ts:384, 376). The face and eyes are on the head's +x side (room.ts:57-58), and placeOnStand sets an identity rotation (station.ts:340). From the bench camera, which looks down −z, you see the robot's flank. The eyes are not visible; only the small antenna lamp turns orange-red, and the wobble is a few pixels (crops 79, 80). The star burst is 6 'star' particles at the robot's top. In the room view after standing up, the event is a tiny glow (shot 82). The nearest coworker is 5.3 m from the bench, so game.alarm({table},3) on a fuse trip (station.ts:238) reaches no one: the bang has no audience. Passing a TEST gives a small 'Elegant' toast (shot 21), and cheer() bursts 12 confetti 1.8 m behind the table, out of frame. The most entertaining beats in the room are mostly lost. This breaks DR-47 (the device shows its state readably), DR-28 (failure shows its cause in the world first) and DR-11/DR-04 (juicy moments, the world reacts).
findings.fix:
(1) In placeOnStand, keep the body's rotation, but yaw the head group by −π/2 so the face screen looks at the bench (+z). Expose `head` from robotMesh and restore it to 0 in startDrive.
(2) In reboot(), spin the head 360° over 0.8 s, show 3 orbiting star sprites for the dizzy duration, and flash the face screen material red as well as the eyes.
(3) Move one mechanic NPC to about (2.4, −3.6), within 3 m of the bench, so trips and arcs make someone jump (src/levels/garage.ts npcs).
(4) On a TEST pass, burst confetti at boardPoint(0, 0) inside the bench frustum (cheer() with `at`), and make the toast tier word bigger, or show a stamped 'ELEGANT' decal on the board for 1.5 s.
findings.verify: Retake garage-play-79/80 at +0.95 s and +1.35 s after an empty PULSE. Both red eyes must be visible from the bench camera; measure red-pixel area > 150 px. In a test after a reversed-diode short, snapshot().alarmed ≥ 1 within 0.5 s.
findings.verify_reason: Crop 79 shows the robot's flank from the bench camera: cargo bin and head side, antenna lamp orange-red, eyes not visible. The code agrees: face and eyes are at the head's local +x (room.ts:57-58), placeOnStand sets an identity rotation (station.ts:340), and the bench camera looks down −z. The nearest NPC (−3.6, −6.3) is 5.27 m from the table, and game.alarm radius is 3 (station.ts:225, 238), so nobody reacts. I did not separately verify the claim that TEST-pass confetti is out of frame. Fix (1) (head yaw −π/2 so +x maps to +z) is geometrically right.
extra_evidence: src/levels/garage.ts:20-22 (npc positions; distance to table 5.27 m)

findings.title: Grades can't go below A: time limit 420 s is 10× the clean solve, and overall = best of three
findings.problem: GarageBench.limits = {time:420, damage:1, cost:≈3.0} (station.ts:77), and grade() returns the best of the three axes (src/sim/grade.ts:6). The clean solve finishes at 46.5 s, about 39 s of play. My chaos run (one smashed crate, cost 8) and my error run (a short, a reversed capacitor and a failed TEST: mistakes 3) both stay far under 420 s, so both grade A overall, with damage and cost at C. A player who trips the fuse, vents the capacitor, fails tests and wrecks the room gets the same medal as one who reasons it out. The grade carries no signal, and the 'experiments cost damage' rule (a PULSE with a backwards diode counts a mistake) only lowers an axis nobody sees. This breaks DR-07 (each axis is tuned per room) and DR-38 (tiers and grades reward understanding).
findings.fix:
Set limits.time to about 2.5× a thoughtful first solve, e.g. 150 s. Keep damage at 1–2.
Don't charge a PULSE short as a mistake. Count only failed TESTs, because PULSE is the free 'look' (station.ts:219-220). Shorts can still cost the 'no tripped fuse' bonus.
For the room as a whole, consider the product-owner-level question in DR-07 (best-of-three vs. median). At minimum, make the result card show which axis carried the grade.
findings.verify: Unit test: grade(43, 3, 8, garage.limits) is not A on every axis. Clean spec: still all A with time ≤ 150 s.
findings.verify_reason: Reproduced. My run had a failed TEST plus a dead short (mistakes 2 → damage 2) and cost 3.7 against a limit of about 2. It finished at 1:02 and the result card showed time A, damage B, cost B, overall A (verify-16, log 'result ... A'). grade.ts:6 takes the best of the three, and limits.time 420 (station.ts:77) is about 7–9× the solve time, so the time axis always carries an A.
extra_evidence: verify log: won t=62.9 damage 2 cost 3.7 → overall A

findings.title: No chaos route, no chaos bonus, and no cable: throwing the robot onto the stand doesn't count, and all three bonuses are bench metrics
findings.problem: The robot only counts as 'on the stand' through station.dropped(), which game.ts calls only on a deliberate E release (src/game.ts:210). Throwing it with Q never triggers the check. I threw the robot from 3 m (02-wrong.mjs): it flew over the bench and landed upside-down by the tool chest, nothing happened and it had to be fetched again (shots 43, 44). The level has obstacles:[] (src/levels/garage.ts:28), and the bonuses are 'every fix reliable', 'elegant' and 'no failed test / no fuse' (station.ts:101-104), all bench numbers. Nothing in the 220-prop room is worth knocking over, and no physical bonus can be found in the world. The room also has no cable at all: rope.maxLength 10 with length 0, and the cable is hidden for stations (game.ts:92/104). The bench harness is a static TubeGeometry (room.ts:81-82). So the star mechanic of the game is absent from a room about wiring. This breaks DR-01 (a chaos route that finishes the job), DR-10 (a findable chaos bonus) and DR-05 (each job involves a physical cable act), and AGENTS 4 and 5.
findings.fix:
(1) Chaos shortcut: in GarageBench.update(), if the robot body is dynamic, not held, at rest (linvel < 0.3) and within 1.6 m of STAND, call the same placeOnStand path with a 'thunk' and dust burst, so a lob onto the rolling road works. Add a bonus: 'Land the robot on the stand from 3 m away'.
(2) Cable act: replace the static harness with a short real lead (Rope, about 4 m) that Pip drags from the stand's socket to the bench's harness port with F. It is finite and shows strain, and the robot isn't 'wired' until it's plugged in. For job 3, the star ground could be Pip dragging the controller's ground lead to the battery post (R4B redesign).
(3) Delivery bonus: 'The robot delivers without bumping a parcel', or the reverse, 'bowl over the parcel stack at (−10, −3.2) on its route'. Place the parcels on the lane on purpose.
findings.verify: New spec 'robot garage: throw the robot onto the stand': hold robot, face the stand at 2.5 m, press KeyQ, advance(2), expect station.onStand true. Check snapshot().rope.maxLength > 0 and that a cable is visible at the game camera.
findings.verify_reason: Code-confirmed. station.dropped is only called from the E release in interact() (game.ts:210), and the throw branch (game.ts:182) never calls it. garage.ts:28 has obstacles:[], and all three bonuses are bench metrics (station.ts:101-104). The snapshot shows rope {length 0, maxLength 10}, and the cable is hidden for stations (game.ts:92). The thrown robot landed upside-down by the tool chest (garage-play-44). RULES.md DR-01 and DR-05 list this as a known station-room gap, still true here. Fix (1) is technically wrong: the Q throw applies mass×8 horizontal and mass×5 vertical impulse (game.ts:182), so about 8 m/s. A lob from 3 m overshoots the stand by metres (shot 44), and 'at rest within 1.6 m of STAND' would almost never fire.
findings.fix_correction: For the chaos shortcut, catch the robot in flight: in GarageBench.update(), if the un-held dynamic robot's horizontal distance to STAND is < 1.2 m while y < 1.6 (or on contact with the stand's collider), snap it with placeOnStand. Alternatively, scale the throw impulse down for items heavier than about 5 kg so a 3 m lob lands near the stand. A rest-distance check alone won't trigger.

findings.title: Phone 390×844: the bench is cut off at both ends, the toast covers PULSE and TEST, and keyboard prompts show on touch
findings.problem: At 390×844 the bench view widens to distance × clamp(1.25/aspect, 1, 2.1), which isn't enough for the 4.3 m table. In shot 72 the 12 V battery and fuse are cut off at the left, and the parts tray at the right: TVS 33 V and 1000 µF are only partly visible and hard to tap. The 'Caught it…' toast sits over the PULSE button and half the TEST pod. The station panel collapses to its title, so the job ask isn't readable. Prompts still show keyboard keys ('1–5 Change the parts', 'Esc Stand up') on a touch device. The survey (shot 71) crops both side walls, and the dock and charging bays are only partly visible. On a phone, job 2 (which needs the TVS) and job 3 (if you try the capacitor) involve tapping half-visible tiles behind HUD. This breaks DR-21 (the survey shows the whole room on a phone) and DR-22 (controls are consistent), and NEXT_STEPS §1 / R3B A12 ('check every bench at 390×844') is still open for the garage.
findings.fix:
- Add an optional portrait `view` to the station (src/stations/types.ts), e.g. {distance:6.8, pitch:1.05, lookX:0} plus a portrait clamp up to 2.6, or move the parts tray onto two rows in front of the board when cam.aspect < 1.
- In ui.css, under body[data-bench] with max-width 600px, dock the .station-toast at the top, below the card, never over the bottom 40 % of the canvas.

findings.verify: Retake garage-play-71/72 at 390×844. All five part tiles, the battery, PULSE and TEST are fully on screen and not under any HUD element. The survey shows all four walls.

findings.title: Text load: the failed-TEST toast is ~45 words and stays up ~16 s, 77 V is shown three times, and job-irrelevant readings are listed
findings.problem: say() keeps a toast for max(4, chars × 0.06) s (station.ts:418). The failed-TEST explanation for a capacitor-only fit is about 270 characters (logic.ts:182-183), so it stays on screen for about 16 s. It covers the bottom of the bench view (shot 51) and follows the player into the room view after standing up (shot 53). Shot 16 shows 'PEAK 77 V' on the scope, 'Stop spike 77V' in the panel and '…spiked to 77 V…' in the toast at the same time (a known DR-41 fail, still present). The panel also lists 'Start sag 0.30 V' in green during jobs 1 and 2, where the sag is irrelevant, so it reads as a passing item to tick. In job 3 it lists the stop spike and current off. Every caption repeats every number ('Clean stop: spike 34 V, current off in 0.44 ms, start sag 0.30 V. TEST it.'). This is far over DR-40's ~25 words, and it buries the one new idea per job under numbers. The garage's own world cues (beads, arc, scope trace) are good enough to carry more of this.
findings.fix:
- Cap toast life at 4 s, clamp(3, chars × 0.03, 5).
- Hide the toast in setActive(false), when standing up.
- Shorten problems[] to one sentence with the cause, e.g. 'No path for the coil's current: the switch broke down at 77 V.' Move the capacitor aside to the paused-panel .profile.
- Drop the numbers from captionFor: the scope readout and panel already show them. Say 'Clean stop. TEST it.' or 'Reset at shutdown.'
- In updatePanel, list only the rows the current job grades: job 1 the spike, job 2 the spike and current off, job 3 the sag.
findings.verify: Word count of the visible HUD text (card + pill + toast + panel, outside the scope) in retakes of shots 16 and 51 is ≤ 30. A toast is never visible after leaving the bench. Each value appears once.
findings.verify_reason: Reproduced. The capacitor-only failed-TEST toast is 273 characters, so 16.4 s by station.ts:418. It was still visible at +8 s and +14 s, and after Esc in the room view (verify-09). setActive(false) doesn't hide it (station.ts:334). After the empty PULSE, 77 V shows three times: scope 'PEAK 77 V', panel 'Stop spike 77V' and toast '…spiked to 77 V…' (verify-07). 'Start sag 0.30 V' appears in green during job 1 (verify-07).
extra_evidence: verify log: toast len 273, still shown at +8 s, after Esc, +14 s

findings.title: Fuse-trip state: the scope says 'reset the FUSE' (there is no reset), the cooling timer is frozen, and the prompt offers 'P Fuse cooling'
findings.problem:
With a backwards diode, PULSE trips the PTC fuse. That is good physics, and it self-resets after 2.5 s (station.ts:237, 348). But:
- The scope prints 'Fix the backwards part, reset the FUSE' (station.ts:289). It gives away the fix, which goes against 'messages say why, never the fix', and it names a FUSE reset action that doesn't exist. This is left over from R3B N3 'click FUSE'.
- The panel row reads 'Fuse cooling 2.5 s' and never counts down. updatePanel's change key (station.ts:424) doesn't include `cooling`, so the row stays frozen: 2.5 s at t=15.3 and again at t=16.5 (shots 47, 48).
- prompt() returns {key:'P', text:'Fuse cooling'} (station.ts:461), a key prompt for a state where P does nothing but a 'hm' (station.ts:215).
- The fuse itself is a 0.11 m disc that glows red, visible but about 15 px at the bench camera.
findings.fix:
- Change the scope text to 'Short across the battery' with the sub-line 'The fuse resets itself when it cools'.
- Add `this.cooling.toFixed(1)` to the updatePanel key, or render a shrinking ring around the fuse disc instead of a text row.
- Change the prompt to {key:'…', text:'Fuse cooling'}, or return null so the hover hint shows.
- Scale the fuse disc ×1.6 and add a small heat-shimmer sprite while it's hot.
findings.verify: After a reversed-diode PULSE, the panel countdown text changes between advance(0.5) steps. The scope contains no 'reset'. The prompt key isn't 'P'.
findings.verify_reason: Reproduced. After a reversed-diode PULSE, the prompt reads 'P Fuse cooling', and the panel row reads 'cooling 2.5 s' at +0.3 s, +0.9 s and +1.5 s (verify log; verify-11), because updatePanel's key omits cooling (station.ts:424). The scope string 'Fix the backwards part, reset the FUSE' is at station.ts:289.
extra_evidence: verify log fuse0 / fuse+0.6 / fuse+1.2 all 'cooling 2.5 s'

findings.title: Robot identity: the prompt calls it 'the cart', there's an identical teal decoy robot on the next pad, and a yellow cart near spawn also says 'Grab the cart'
findings.problem: The job robot is spec kind 'cart' (src/levels/garage.ts:8), and NAMES maps cart→'cart' (src/ui/objectives.ts:58), so the prompt at the robot reads 'E Grab the cart' (shot 06) while the card says 'Carry the delivery robot'. The yellow mail cart at (−1, 6.6) right beside spawn (garage.ts:19) also prompts 'Grab the cart', which makes it the likeliest first grab for a new player. Two of the three charging pads hold decor robots (room.ts:85-87). The one at 4.4 is the same TEAL as the job robot and sits right next to it, but it's a fixed solid, so E only shrugs (shot 42). Only the marker tells them apart, and the marker is a 25 px unoutlined pale cone against a cream wall (crop 90). This breaks DR-50 (one name per thing), DR-17 (no false affordances that look like the job item) and DR-42 (the prompt names the current step's object).
findings.fix:
In objectives.ts promptFor, prefer a name by id: add `const ID_NAMES={robot:'delivery robot'}` and use it before NAMES[kind]. Or let the station supply the walking prompt when nearest().spec.id==='robot': 'E Pick up the delivery robot'.
Make the decor robots read as 'charging, not this one': give them a plugged-in cable from the wall charger and closed sleepy eyes (eyes material toon('#34424a')). Give the job robot a red '!' fault light or a blinking red antenna lamp at start.
Re-colour the spawn-side mail cart away from job yellow.
findings.verify: At the robot, the .prompt-pill text contains 'robot'. Retake garage-play-01: the job robot is distinguishable from the decor robots in a greyscale squint (DR-43), e.g. by a blinking red lamp.
findings.verify_reason: Reproduced. At the robot the pill reads 'E Grab the cart' while the card says 'delivery robot' (verify log 'at robot'). NAMES maps cart→'cart' (objectives.ts:58), and a yellow cart spawns at (−1, 6.6) (garage.ts:19). The decor robots are fixed solids, not props (room.ts:85-87). I also found the same wrong name in two more places. After the robot is fixed on the stand, the room prompt still offers 'E Grab the cart' for it (garage-play-75). While it drives, the prompt offers 'E Grab the cart' for the moving robot (verify log drive 3-9).
extra_evidence: verify log 'at robot': 'E Grab the cart'
mockups/review5/shots/garage-play-75-behind-bench-low.jpg (fixed robot on stand still prompts 'Grab the cart')
verify log drive 3-9: 'E Grab the cart' during delivery
findings.fix_correction: Also exclude the robot from nearest() once onStand or driving, since it is then Fixed or kinematic and grabbing it does nothing useful.

findings.title: Job yellow and cable-job props in a cable-free room: yellow crates, a yellow reel, extra reels from the 'parts' recipe
findings.problem: The garage clutter palette includes '#ffc629' (job yellow, garage.ts:31), and the recipes list 'parts' twice. Each 'parts' cluster adds a reel and a splitter (src/levels/clutter.ts:45). A hand-placed yellow reel stands at (−4.4, 6.8) (garage.ts:12), and the dolly carries another. The start and survey shots show tall yellow crate stacks (left wall), yellow boxes on carts, a yellow cart near spawn, and two or three cable reels (white by the rug, yellow front-left, a yellow reel on the dolly at right; shots 01, 02). This room has no cable job. Reels and splitters are the most recognisable job items from the cable floors, so they are pure false affordances here, and the job-yellow clutter competes with the robot's yellow lid and the pale marker. This breaks DR-17 (no false affordances) and DR-45 (no decorative clutter in job yellow).
findings.fix:
- Remove '#ffc629' from garage clutter.colors and use kraft or teal-grey instead.
- Replace the 'parts' recipe in the garage with a garage-specific recipe: wheel stacks, toolboxes, oil cans, spare robot heads.
- Change the hand-placed reel at garage.ts:12 to a toolbox or tyre.
- Keep yellow for the robot's lid and the stand's hazard edge only.
findings.verify: Retake garage-play-01/02: count props within 25 ΔE of #ffc629 that aren't the robot or the stand. Target 0. There are no reels or splitters in the room.
findings.verify_reason: Code-confirmed. '#ffc629' is in the garage clutter colours (garage.ts:31), a yellow reel is placed at garage.ts:12, and the 'parts' recipe adds a reel and a splitter (clutter.ts:45), listed twice in the garage recipes. The survey (verify-10) and room views show yellow crate stacks and yellow and white reels front-left and on the dolly, in a room with no cable job.

findings.title: Bench key leaks: Tab toggles a hidden survey, Space makes seated Pip jump, and hover hints show keys for non-actions
findings.problem:
At the bench, game.ts:164 passes any key the station doesn't use through to the walking handlers:
- Tab toggles `survey` invisibly (the bench camera overrides it), so standing up lands the player in the zoomed-out survey (shots 52, 53).
- Space triggers jump while seated: Pip rose to y 2.0, airborne, with the arms pose (02-wrong.mjs log).
- R reloads the level instantly without confirmation (restart action), which is easy to hit next to the bench's F, G, P and 1–5 keys.
- hoverHint shows 'S It does not fit here' and 'A Empty socket' (station.ts:445), key pills for actions that do nothing.
This breaks DR-22 (no game key acts while a menu-like mode is open) and DR-19 (every key prompt is a real action).
findings.fix:
In the bench branch of game.ts:164, after station.key() returns false, `e.preventDefault(); return;` for everything except Escape/E (handled) and the pause key. In particular, don't add Tab, Space or R to keys or actions while atBench.
In hoverHint, return key '' for the 'does not fit' and 'empty socket' texts.
findings.verify: Playwright: at the bench press Tab, Space and R. Expect the page not to reload, player.y to stay at about 0.77, and after Esc the camera zoom to equal homeZoom (not 44).
findings.verify_reason: Reproduced. Tab at the bench, then Esc, landed in the full survey view (verify-10). Space at the bench raised Pip to y 1.6 (log 'space at bench'). The code passes unhandled keys through at game.ts:164-166, including KeyR→restart (location.reload) with no confirmation. I did not press R to avoid losing the run, so that part is code-only. The hoverHint key pills for non-actions are at station.ts:445.
extra_evidence: verify log 'space at bench': player.y 1.6 while atBench

findings.title: Failing readings in the bench panel aren't red: class 'no' is styled neutral grey, and only passes are coloured
findings.problem: updatePanel's row() emits class 'ok' or 'no' (station.ts:428), but ui.css only colours li.ok (green) and li.bad (red). li.no is ink-2 grey semi-bold (src/ui/ui.css:225). So the 77 V spike that just reset the controller shows in plain dark text, while the irrelevant 0.30 V sag shows reassuring green (crop 81, shot 16). The eye goes to the green item and reads 'that's fine'. It's a small fix that strengthens 'see it, not read it'. Also, on the job-3 scope the 'resets below 4.4 V' label is drawn on the trace and is partly overwritten by it (shot 24).
findings.fix:
In station.ts:428, emit `ok?'ok':'bad'` for graded failing rows, keeping 'no' for neutral (stale) rows. Or add `.station-panel .build li.no b{color:#c0392b}` if 'no' is meant as fail; check the other stations first.
In drawScope, draw the hline label below the line when the trace's minimum is within 40 px above it (or always at the left edge).
findings.verify: Retake crop 81 after an empty PULSE: 'Stop spike 77 V' renders in rgb(192,57,43).
findings.verify_reason: Confirmed. row() emits 'no' (station.ts:428) and ui.css:225 styles li.no as ink-2 grey. After the empty PULSE, 'Stop spike 77V' is dark text and 'Start sag 0.30V' is green (verify-07). In job 3 the failing '0.90V' sag is neutral, while the passing 34 V and 0.44 ms rows are green (verify-13). On the job-3 scope, the 'resets below 4.4 V' label sits on the trace (verify-13). The 'no' class is shared by the arcade, observatory, qfn and spectrum panels, so a CSS-only change affects all of them, as the fix notes.

findings.title: Step 2 'Sit at the garage bench' can tick before step 1, flashing out of order
findings.problem: Step 2 is `done:()=>this.active||this.logged.length>0` (station.ts:98), so sitting at the bench before the robot is placed (a likely wrong move) latches step 2 done. The step bell rings, the card flashes 'Sit at the garage bench (E)' and the second progress dot turns green while the first is still hollow (shot 40, log 'sat'). Then the bench says 'E Fetch the robot' and P gives 'The robot is still on its charging pad.' Later the step is skipped entirely. The progress dots and bell (the only reward signal on the card) fire for a non-achievement.
findings.fix: `done:()=>this.onStand&&(this.active||this.logged.length>0)`.
findings.verify: Sit at the bench before carrying the robot: the objective card's second dot isn't 'done' and no bell sounds.
findings.verify_reason: Shot 40 shows dot 1 hollow and dot 2 green after sitting before the robot is placed. station.ts:98 done = active||logged, and objectives.ts latches each step independently. The one-line fix is correct.

findings.title: Pip hides behind the bench and scope at the test stand, and behind crate stacks; neither fades
findings.problem: Step 1 ends behind the bench, at the stand (0.7, −4.45). With a low or default orbit from the front, Pip there is hidden from the chest down by the 1 m bench plus the scope cabinet (shots 75, 76). Only the hat shows, and the stand and robot are hidden too. Near the tool chest, the clutter crate stacks hide Pip's legs (shot 77). The occlusion fade only covers `occluders` (pillars) with one ray to p.y+0.4 (game.ts:386-388), so bench, scope and crates never fade. This is the global DR-12 known issue, confirmed here at a required location.
findings.fix: Register the bench body, the scope cabinet and the TEST STAND sign as occluders in buildBench (push them into game.occluders with transparent toon materials). Cast three rays (feet, chest, head) as DR-12 asks.
findings.verify: Retake garage-play-75/76: Pip's body pixels are ≥ 70 % visible.
findings.verify_reason: Shot 75 shows Pip behind the bench with only his head and shoulders visible above the bench and scope, and the stand and robot hidden. game.occluders is filled only by decor.ts pillars and walls (and spectrum's room), with one ray to p.y+0.4 (game.ts:387-388). Nothing in garage/station.ts or room.ts registers an occluder.
extra_evidence: grep occluders: src/levels/decor.ts:48,55 and src/stations/spectrum/room.ts only

findings.title: Draw calls 1156 at the game camera (and in survey)
findings.problem: snapshot() at the start reported drawCalls 1156 for 111 props (fps 60 on the host GPU). The DR-24 target is ≤ about 250. R3B measured 953, so dense clutter (max 220) has pushed it up. That's fine on this GPU, but a phone or iGPU will drop quality via adaptQuality. The bench labels (one canvas texture per sign), the pegboard tools, per-dash lane boxes (room.ts:70-71; about 30 separate meshes) and per-wheel parts on the decor robots are all separate meshes in decorRoot.
findings.fix:
- Merge static decorRoot meshes per material (BufferGeometryUtils.mergeGeometries) after dressGarage.
- Instance the lane dashes (one InstancedMesh).
- Atlas the bench sign labels into one texture.
- Merge decor robot copies.
findings.verify: snapshot().drawCalls ≤ 300 at the start and in survey.
findings.verify_reason: Reproduced: snapshot at the start gave drawCalls 1156, props 111, fps 60. The renderer counts every pass (composer + outlines, game.ts:450), so this is the same metric DR-24 uses. It is well over about 250, but fps holds on the host GPU, so P2 is right.

notes.fun:
What works: the garage has the best 'see the physics' moment in the game. An empty PULSE makes the white-hot arc jump the switch, sparks fly, the robot on the stand wobbles, and cyan beads stall at the switch. A diode makes the beads keep circling the little motor-and-diode loop and fade, which shows the concept on the copper (shots 14, 18). The robot driving its painted lane to the dock is a charming payoff, and the scope trace drawing across is satisfying. The first spectacle (the arc) arrives about 15 s in for a clean player.

What doesn't: the fun sits on a 1 m square of bench, mostly too small to see. The reboot faces away from the camera, the pass celebration is a tiny 'Elegant' toast, and nobody in the room reacts to the bang. Around the bench, the 22 × 16 m room with 111 props has no reason to touch anything. There's no cable, no chaos shortcut (a thrown robot doesn't count), no physical bonus, and the drive ends with 9 s of watching. When the robot bulldozed Pip 4 m down its lane there was no reaction at all, which wastes free slapstick. Grading gives A regardless of how many fuses you trip. Clean solve about 39 s of play (46.5 s with my camera checks), plus about 9.5 s of drive.
notes.playability:
The clean route is smooth and short: about 2 s from spawn to the robot, about 3 s to carry it around the bench's right end, and about 2 s to sit. The clutter lanes keep the robot route and walking route clear; every walkTo arrived with no stalls. g.audit(0.02) is empty, and there were zero console errors across 5 scripts. The robot can be thrown, re-grabbed, dropped on wheel stacks and recovered; I found no soft-lock. A wedged robot stayed reachable, because the nearest grab tolerance is generous. The real problems:
- A/S/D at the bench remove fitted parts, which matters because players reach for WASD.
- The carried robot tips on its side beside Pip's head.
- At phone size the bench tray and battery are cut off and the toast covers PULSE.
- Tab, Space and R leak through at the bench.
- Pip disappears behind the bench and scope at the stand.
Mouse play works well: hover enlarges parts and sockets, and clicking picks, fits and flips. The fuse self-resets, so there's no dead end after a short.
notes.teaching: (Secondary for this key.) The model is truthful and the shutdown visualisation is excellent. But the act is mostly a menu pick: each part fits only one socket, and the prompt names the socket key. So 'where protection goes' (the topology the sockets are named after) is never chosen, and cycling 1–5 + P brute-forces each job without penalty. Job 2's failure ('too slow for the stop line') has no physical consequence: the robot doesn't coast past a line, so the idea lives only in a millisecond number. Job 3's ground-route idea is hidden behind a tiny lever while the prompt points at the parts tray.
notes.clarity:
The objective card is concise and the bench reads cleanly at 1440×900. The board's left-to-right battery → fuse → motor → node → switch → controller layout, the dashed '+' empty sockets, the glow on the legal socket and 'Robot not on the stand' on the scope are all good no-text cues.
Problems:
- The marker rides on the carried robot instead of showing the stand.
- The prompt calls the robot 'the cart', and there are two identical-looking teal robots and a yellow 'cart' by spawn.
- '1–5 Change the parts' misleads in job 3.
- 'P Fuse cooling' and 'reset the FUSE' name non-actions.
- Failing panel values aren't red.
- The toast text is long (about 45 words for about 16 s) and repeats every number (77 V three times).
- The step-2 dot can tick before step 1.
- Job-yellow clutter and leftover cable reels add noise around the one yellow-lidded job item.
notes.models:
(Seen while playing.) The robot model is cute and readable on its pad. The bench board, scope cabinet and test pod read well. Issues:
- The carry pose (tilted robot at head height, pierced by the marker).
- The face points +x, so the bench camera never sees the eyes.
- The decor robots duplicate the job robot's look.
- The 'TEST STAND' plaque floats on a thin post behind the stand.
- The arc bloom washes out the SWITCH label for about 0.5 s (DR-66 known).
